children: August was a tough month for Ford Motor Co. (F, Financials) and the pain spread far beyond the general U.S. sales decrease.
The company sold 170,681 automobiles in the month, down 10.3 percent from a year earlier. The more urgent challenge was electric cars.
Ford's EV sales dropped 79.4% year over year, while hybrid sales dropped 19.9%. That makes the EV decrease the most important figure for investors.

Ford has invested considerably to expand its electric vehicle business, but the latest sales figures illustrate the inconsistent demand as the firm seeks to combine its traditional vehicle selection with newer electric vehicles.
The hybrid fade also trims some of the cushion Ford has counted on as consumers slowly move toward electrified vehicles. The August data offer a simple question for investors.
If demand for EVs is this weak, Ford may have to rely more heavily on its profitable gasoline-powered trucks and SUVs and rethink how aggressively it spends on electric capacity.
The next catalyst will be September sales and whether EV demand stabilizes or we see continued downturn into the last few months of the year.

title: Ford's EV Sales Just Collapsed 79% in August
